title: Consumer Protection Act 2019 — Rights and Remedies
content:
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the older 1986 Act to strengthen consumer rights and streamline dispute resolution in India. It applies to all goods and services, including e-commerce transactions, online payments, digital platforms, and direct selling.

Who is a Consumer: A consumer is any person who buys goods or avails services for consideration (payment), whether online or offline. A person who buys goods for resale or commercial purpose is generally excluded, except for self-employment livelihood.

Consumer Rights: The Act guarantees six basic rights: (1) Right to Safety, (2) Right to Information, (3) Right to Choose, (4) Right to be Heard, (5) Right to Seek Redressal, and (6) Right to Consumer Education.

Unfair Trade Practices & Deficiency in Service: Consumers can file complaints against seller/service providers for defective goods, deficiency in service, unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, overcharging above MRP, or failure to refund money for returned goods or non-delivered services.

E-Commerce Rules: Under Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, e-commerce entities must disclose country of origin, seller details, return/exchange policies, grievance officer details, and refund mechanisms. Sellers cannot impose cancellation charges unless identical charges are borne by the seller for cancellation.

Three-Tier Redressal Commission:
1. District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (District Commission): Claims up to ₹1 Crore.
2. State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (State Commission): Claims above ₹1 Crore up to ₹10 Crore.
3. National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC): Claims above ₹10 Crore.

Filing a Complaint (e-Daakhil): Complaints can be filed online via the e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) or physically in the District Commission where the consumer resides or works, regardless of where the seller operates.

Limitation Period: A consumer complaint must be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose.

Remedies Available: District/State Commissions can order replacement of goods, refund of price paid along with interest, compensation for financial/mental agony, removal of defects, and payment of legal costs.
